results.title: Verda Review 2026 | EuropeanStack
highlights:
Finnish GPU cloud, formerly DataCrunch, running AI training and inference on 100% renewable Nordic power

...

Verda, known until November 2025 as DataCrunch, is a Helsinki-founded GPU cloud provider offering on-demand NVIDIA GPU instances, serverless inference containers, and multi-node clusters for AI training and inference. Founded in 2020 by Ruben Bryon, it runs data centres in Finland and Iceland on 100% renewable power and has submitted a bid to host one of the EU's AI Gigafactories.

...

## Pricing

### Spot Instances

Pay-as-you-go

- H100 SXM5 from $1.63/hour
- B200 SXM6 from $3.06/hour
- Roughly 50% cheaper than on-demand
- Can be reclaimed with short notice

### On-Demand Instances

Pay-as-you-go

- H100 SXM5 from $3.25/hour, H200 from $4.00/hour
- B200 SXM6 from $6.11/hour, GB300 from $8.62/hour
- NVMe, shared filesystem, and registry storage at $0.20/GiB-month
- No long-term commitment required

...

Is Verda the same company as DataCrunch?

Yes. DataCrunch rebranded to Verda on 17 November 2025 and migrated its site to verda.com. It is the same Helsinki-founded, Finland- and Iceland-based GPU cloud provider, just under a new name and broader AI-cloud positioning.

...

For most of its history, this company was called DataCrunch — a Helsinki-founded GPU cloud provider that quietly built a reputation among ML engineers for cheap H100 access without the AWS markup. Ruben Bryon founded it in 2020, and for five years it stayed a well-regarded but relatively niche player, the kind of provider you found through a Hacker News thread rather than a marketing budget. On 17 November 2025, that changed: DataCrunch became Verda, migrated to verda.com, and repositioned itself from a GPU rental service into what it calls a "full-stack AI cloud."

...

Verda prices in USD across on-demand, spot, and reserved tiers rather than fixed monthly plans, which is standard for GPU cloud infrastructure. On-demand H100 SXM5 runs $3.25/hour. The same instance on spot pricing drops to $1.63/hour but can be reclaimed with short notice, so it suits fault-tolerant training jobs rather than latency-sensitive inference. Reserved instances with a 2-year commitment cut up to 25% off on-demand rates, which is meaningful for teams with predictable, sustained GPU demand.

highlights:

1. Platform overview: packet.ai vs Verda

Run it on a GPU

B200 from $4.25/hr, RTX 4090 from $0.39/hr. Hourly, no contract.

Verda is the new name for DataCrunch, the Helsinki-based GPU cloud that runs on renewable energy in Finland and Iceland and has quietly built one of the broadest Blackwell rate cards in Europe: B200, B300, GB300, alongside H200, H100, A100, RTX Pro 6000 and L40S. Its distinguishing feature is a published spot tier at 50% of on-demand across the board, plus a serverless container product.

...

### What Verda offers

Verda's published on-demand rates as of late August 2026: GB300 $8.62/hr, B300 $7.50/hr, B200 $6.11/hr, H200 SXM $4.00/hr, H100 SXM $3.25/hr, RTX Pro 6000 (96GB) $1.89/hr, A100 SXM 80GB $1.79/hr, A100 40GB $1.29/hr, L40S $1.37/hr, RTX 6000 Ada $1.04/hr, RTX A6000 $0.61/hr. Spot is 50% of on-demand on every card (B200 $3.06, H200 $2.00, RTX Pro 6000 about $0.95). Reserved terms from 1 to 24 months discount 2–25%.

- Per-second billing, no minimum commitment; instances from 1× to 8× on most cards
- Renewable-powered data centres in Finland and Iceland; ISO-certified; strong EU residency story
- Serverless containers priced separately (H100 $3.58/hr, L40S $1.51/hr) with spot at about half
- Confidential-computing variants of B200 and RTX Pro 6000 at a small premium

...

What Verda has that packet.ai does not: H100, H200 and B300 on the rate card today, a true spot tier for checkpointed training that can beat Dynamic on the largest cards, confidential-computing variants, and Nordic renewable-powered residency. If your workload is Hopper-class and can tolerate interruption, Verda's spot tier is genuinely hard to beat. If you need non-interruptible capacity at a price below anyone's spot rate, packet.ai's Dynamic tier does that on the RTX Pro 6000 specifically.

Billing is hourly; the one monthly plan is 2× B200 Dedicated at $11,665.40/mo. There are no platform fees and no ingress charges; egress is $0.04/GB. Local storage is included with every instance, from 150 GB (RTX PRO 6000 Dynamic) to 2.8 TB (8× B200 Dedicated). Dynamic instances are SSH-ready in under five minutes, Dedicated in five to ten. Capacity is live in the US (California, Virginia, Texas, Oregon) and Europe (Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Paris, London, Dublin). H100 SXM, H200 and RTX 5090 are on the notify list.

results.title: Same GPU, Eight Clouds: The Real Price Spread
results.author: Ansh Saxena
highlights:
Every number here comes from a single snapshot of our own public marketplace feed, taken on August 4, 2026. It covers 638 offers across 8 providers: Vast.ai (338 offers), SimplePod (197), Massed Compute (39), Akash (29), Vultr (24), Verda (5, then trading as DataCrunch), Hyperstack (5) and Hot Aisle (1).

Every price is normalized to dollars per GPU per hour. That normalization is the part that goes wrong most often in published comparisons, so to be explicit: for almost every provider the feed's `price` is the total for the offer and the divisor is the GPU count. Akash is the exception: its listed price is already per-GPU and must not be divided. Get this backwards and you publish numbers that are wrong by exactly the GPU count, which is how a $0.20 card becomes a $1.80 card in a table nobody double-checks.

...

This is one point in time. Availability moves hourly, and a provider that looks cheapest today may have nothing in stock tomorrow. Treat it as a snapshot, not a league table.

...

| GPU | Offers | Cheapest provider (median) | Most expensive (median) | Cross-provider gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 5090 | 80 | Akash $0.420 | Vast.ai $0.708 | 1.7x |
| RTX 4090 | 78 | Akash $0.336 | Vast.ai $0.680 | 2.0x |
| V100 | 70 | SimplePod $0.070 | Vast.ai $0.317 | 4.5x |
| A100 | 38 | Vast.ai $1.101 | Verda $1.790 | 1.6x |
| RTX 3090 | 36 | SimplePod $0.160 | Vast.ai $0.274 | 1.7x |
| RTX PRO 6000 | 19 | SimplePod $1.393 | Massed Compute $2.190 | 1.6x |
| H100 | 9 | Massed Compute $2.590 | Vast.ai $3.420 | 1.3x |
| L40S | 8 | Vast.ai $0.851 | Massed Compute $0.880 | 1.0x |

...

The wide ones are all consumer cards: RTX 5090, 5080, 4090, 3090, 4070 Super. The tight ones are almost all datacenter parts: H100 (1.3x cross-provider), H200 (1.3x), L40S (1.0x), RTX PRO 6000 (1.6x), A6000 on Massed Compute (1.1x).

...

2. The B200 has one supplier in this feed. Eight offers, all Vast.ai, $5.095 to $7.635 per GPU-hour. Newest silicon means no competitive floor yet: you're paying whatever the small number of people who have them decide to charge. The MI300X is thinner still: a single node.

results.title: Cheapest H100 and B200 Cloud: CoreWeave vs Nebius vs Lambda vs Crusoe · Aliteq
results.author: Aliteq Team
highlights:
On each provider's own pricing page on Nov 3, 2026, Crusoe had the cheapest on-demand H100 ($3.90 a GPU-hour, rising to $4.50 on Dec 1) and Lambda the cheapest B200 ($6.69). CoreWeave was the most expensive on demand, but its fixed spot prices undercut everyone's on-demand rate. The full table, the catches, and where the marketplace tier sits.

...

Which big GPU cloud is cheapest for H100 and B200? On each provider's own pricing page on November 3, 2026: for the H100, Crusoe at $3.90 per GPU-hour on demand, with Lambda a cent behind at $3.99 on an 8-GPU instance. For the B200, Lambda at $6.69 per GPU-hour (8x), well under Nebius ($8.50) and CoreWeave ($8.60). CoreWeave is the most expensive on demand, but if your job can be interrupted its published spot prices ($2.46 an H100, $4.26 a B200, per GPU) undercut everyone's on-demand rate. Two dates to know: Crusoe's own page says its H100 goes to $4.50 on December 1, 2026, which hands the cheapest on-demand H100 to Lambda.

## The short answer (read Nov 3, 2026)

Among CoreWeave, Nebius, Lambda and Crusoe, the cheapest on-demand H100 on November 3, 2026 was Crusoe at $3.90 per GPU-hour, then Lambda at $3.99 (8x instance), Nebius at $4.50 and CoreWeave at $6.16 (an 8-GPU node at $49.24 an hour). Crusoe's page says its H100 rises to $4.50 on December 1, 2026. The cheapest on-demand B200 was Lambda at $6.69 per GPU-hour (8x; $6.99 on one GPU), then Nebius at $8.50 and CoreWeave at $8.60; Crusoe's B200 is contact-sales. For interruptible work, CoreWeave's spot nodes work out to $2.46 per H100 and $4.26 per B200, and Nebius preemptible starts from $0.79 (H100) and $0.99 (B200) at a dynamic rate. Smaller clouds go lower still: Hyperstack listed a B200 at $6.00 and an H100 at $2.50.

results.title: Fireworks is raising on-demand GPU prices up to 30% on September 1 | Beyond the News
highlights:
# Fireworks is raising on-demand GPU prices up to 30% on September 1

Fireworks' current pricing table shows September 1 increases across H100, H200, B200, B300 and GB300 on-demand deployments, with B200 rising from $10 to $13 per GPU-hour. Dedicated training jobs that use the same GPU-hour rates inherit the new economics.

Reviewed and published by Lars Jansen Updated 28 Aug 2026, 10:59 pm NZST 4 min read Copy link

 First published 28 Aug 2026, 10:59 pm NZST 

## Key details

1. The new Fireworks on-demand GPU rates begin September 1, 2026.
2. H100 80GB: $7 → $8 per GPU-hour.
3. H200 141GB: $7 → $8 per GPU-hour.
4. B200 180GB: $10 → $13 per GPU-hour.
5. B300 288GB: $12 → $15 per GPU-hour.
6. GB300 288GB: $18 → $20 per GPU-hour.
7. On-demand deployments are billed per GPU second with no extra startup charges.
8. Region-restricted deployments are priced at a 1.5× premium.
9. Dedicated Training API jobs use the same on-demand GPU-hour pricing.

...

## What changed

Fireworks' current pricing page publishes a two-column transition for its on-demand GPU deployments: prices through August 31 and new rates from September 1, 2026. H100 80GB and H200 141GB increase from $7 to $8 per GPU-hour; B200 180GB rises from $10 to $13; B300 288GB from $12 to $15; and GB300 288GB from $18 to $20. Fireworks bills on-demand deployments per GPU second with no startup charge, and its Dedicated Training API uses the same GPU-hour pricing, so the change affects both dedicated serving and GPU-hour training jobs. Region-restricted deployments continue to carry a 1.5× premium.

...

Dedicated GPU economics can dominate the unit cost of high-volume inference, fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning workloads. These increases range from roughly 11% to 30%, large enough to change break-even points between accelerator generations, serverless APIs and competing GPU clouds. The biggest increase is on B200, where a workload consuming 1,000 GPU-hours per month moves from $10,000 to $13,000 before regional premiums or other services. Teams should therefore benchmark completed-task throughput rather than choosing hardware on hourly price or peak specifications alone.

## The September increase varies materially by accelerator

H100 and H200 move from $7 to $8 per hour, about a 14.3% increase. B200 rises 30% from $10 to $13, B300 rises 25% from $12 to $15 and GB300 rises about 11.1% from $18 to $20. The uneven changes can alter the relative cost ranking of GPUs even when performance remains unchanged.

## Training inherits the same GPU-hour table

Fireworks states that Dedicated Training API jobs are priced per GPU hour using the On-Demand Pricing section. Teams running reinforcement fine-tuning or dedicated training should therefore update both serving and training forecasts, not only inference deployment budgets.

## Per-second billing limits idle waste but not rate exposure

On-demand deployments are billed by the second and do not charge extra startup time, which remains useful for bursty workloads. But sustained fleets still absorb the full hourly increase, and a region-restricted deployment costs 1.5 times the listed rate.

## Hourly price is not total inference cost

A more expensive accelerator can still win if it materially improves throughput, latency or batch efficiency. Builders should compare cost per successful request, training run or completed agent task under the exact model, quantization, context and concurrency they use.

...

## Still unclear

- The pricing page publishes the dated rate transition but does not explain the commercial rationale for each GPU-specific increase.
- Effective cost varies significantly with model serving efficiency, batching, quantization, context length and utilization.
- Enterprise or negotiated contracts may differ from public on-demand pricing.
